findings: Loopback finding resolved: attempt 2 has a non-empty builder delta (anvil/sinks.py closes the HTTPError response so failing API calls no longer leak sockets; new tests/test_live_progress_sink_errors.py; CHANGELOG.md). The surface stays within the authorized set, and anvil/runner.py changes only at the RunRecorder construction (stations=order) and gains no network code.

Secrets (R5): the token is read from os.environ at call time and only goes into the Authorization header (anvil/sinks.py Sink.request). Export error notes are limited to '<type>: HTTP <status>' or '<type>: <ExceptionClassName>' (note_for), and inactive reasons name the variable, never its value. A crashed record's error text is not rendered into the comment. Test test_s9_token_appears_only_in_the_authorization_header and the project sink token tests cover this. All 31 sink tests pass (2 skips are run-bound).

Least privilege for stations: validate_sinks in anvil/config.py refuses a token_env that is missing from STATION_ENV_DENY or listed in runtime.env_keep, so a sink token can never reach a station environment. GH_TOKEN is in the default deny list. This fails closed at load time.

Input handling: the issue number comes only from a ^wo-gh-([0-9]+)$ match, GITHUB_REPOSITORY must match owner/repo, owner_type is limited to user or organization before it is interpolated into the GraphQL query, and owner, number, field and option values are passed as GraphQL variables, not by joining strings. Request URLs must use http or https. The sinks list is validated against an allow list of types and keys, rejecting rather than repairing.

Comment content (R2.6): render_issue_comment emits scalar facts only (ids, pipeline, station names, statuses, counts, cost, timestamps, run link). It includes no prompt, station output, path or environment value other than GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL and GITHUB_RUN_ID, all of which are public.

Non-blocking hardening (low): _find_comment refuses to follow a pagination Link to a host other than the API base. However, urllib's default HTTPRedirectHandler forwards the Authorization header on a cross-host 3xx redirect of a GET. A redirect from the configured API host would carry the token elsewhere. The risk is low because the API host is trusted platform configuration, but an opener that refuses redirects or strips Authorization across hosts would make the same-host guarantee hold for redirects as well as Link headers.

Non-blocking (low): the API base comes from GITHUB_API_URL, as the spec requires (R2.7). Anyone who can set that variable in the line process can direct the token to another host. This matches the existing trust model of the runner environment and is not a regression.

No new dependency (standard library only), no new endpoint or file write outside the run directory, no change to .github/workflows. Export failures never change the verdict: SinkSet.deliver catches every exception and records a note, as required by the frozen export rule.
